title: The "mentions you" chip does nothing, and the number of chips contradicts the sentence above it
surface: Client dashboard → Search & AI visibility → buyer questions list and the engine comparison card (/clients/[id])
whatYouSee: Some questions carry a small "mentions you" chip. It isn't clickable, has no tooltip, doesn't filter the list and doesn't reveal anything. Meanwhile the card above says the comparison excludes the four questions that name you directly — and you can count more chips than that.
whyItsWrong: The chip and the count come from two different classifiers. The chip is set by matching only the client's display name against the prompt text. The "questions that name you" count comes from the pipeline's intent classifier, which matches the full alias set (name, domain, short label) and — critically — returns "comparison" for anything containing alternative / vs / compare BEFORE it checks for the brand name. So "Karos alternatives" is counted as a category question, and is included in the like-for-like comparison, while still wearing a chip that says the opposite. In the other direction a multi-word brand loses its chip on the bare-domain prompt, which the pipeline does count as naming you. The chip count also comes from all questions in the set while the sentence's count comes only from questions an engine actually answered, so the two can diverge again on a partial run. The presenter's own comment documents this divergence as a known follow-up, and it is shipping to clients. On top of that the chip is the only marker on a row that is otherwise inert — there is no way to see what any engine said about that question.
evidence: src/components/seo-geo/presenter.ts:782-788 — chip from `findMention(prompt, insights.roster[0])`
src/components/seo-geo/presenter.ts:771-779 — comment admitting the classifier divergence and naming the follow-up
src/components/seo-geo-panel.tsx:443-447 — chip rendered as inert text
src/components/seo-geo-panel.tsx:365-368 — "excluding the {brandPresence.total} question(s) that name you directly"
src/lib/seo-geo.ts:1036-1045 — classifyIntent: navigational, then comparison (line 1041) BEFORE brand (line 1042)
src/lib/intel/seo-geo.ts:738-741 and 756 — brand/category split driven by classifyIntent
src/lib/seo-geo.ts:547-559 — computePresence counts only prompts with a measured probe
fix: Drive the chip from the persisted per-prompt intent, which is already the single source of truth: in src/components/seo-geo/presenter.ts:782-788 read `insights.intentPrompts` and set the chip when `intent === "brand" || intent === "navigational"`, deleting the display-name match — that makes the chip count equal brandPresence.total by construction. Then either attach an InfoTip (the component already exists in src/components/seo-geo-panel.tsx:34) explaining that the question names your brand and is excluded from the competitor comparison, or turn the row into the per-question expander described in the answer-grid finding.

title: The buyer-questions list is an unpunctuated flat dump, and it hides the competitor roster and the citation leaderboard inside it
surface: Client dashboard → Search & AI visibility → methodology card (/clients/[id])
whatYouSee: One collapsed grey row: "The 20 buyer questions we asked". Open it and you get twenty one-line rows of bare text with no quotation marks, no question marks on many of them ("Top-rated dental clinics", "Karos alternatives", "karoslabs.com", "Karos official site"), no grouping and no hierarchy. Keep scrolling inside that same collapsed row and you find two entirely different sections buried below the questions: who we compare you against, and who the engines quote as sources.
whyItsWrong: Two problems in one card. Structure: the questions are printed as bare text, even though the data needed to structure them already exists and is persisted with a five-way intent taxonomy, and the markdown brief for the same run groups by intent and wraps each question in quotes — the client-facing UI throws that away. Non-questions in the set are not accidental either: the deterministic fallback set deliberately contains bare keyword strings and a bare domain, and the prompt sanitizer never adds terminal punctuation. Information architecture: the competitor roster and the citation leaderboard — both named sections of this report — are children of a disclosure whose label only mentions buyer questions and which is closed by default, so a client asking "who are you comparing me to?" will never find the answer.

title: The citation leaderboard silently truncates, and the whole citation story disappears in the case that matters most
surface: Client dashboard → Search & AI visibility → methodology card → "Who the engines quote as sources" (/clients/[id])
whatYouSee: A list of eight domains with bars. No count, no "show all", no hint there were more. And when nobody was cited at all this run, the entire block — including the line explaining that your site was never cited as a source — simply isn't there, while the engine cards above still say "cited as a source: 0 of 14 answers" with no explanation.
whyItsWrong: The leaderboard is computed with a limit of twelve but rendered with a hard slice of eight and no affordance, so up to four competitor source domains are dropped invisibly. Worse, the client's own citation sentence is nested inside the gate that requires at least one non-client cited domain — so the single most important sentence in the section, the one that says your site was never cited and that earning citations is what moves the score, is exactly the sentence that cannot render when there are no citations at all. The zero state deletes its own explanation.

title: The snapshot date is a bare machine date with no staleness cue, and the client has no way to get the "next snapshot" the report keeps promising
surface: Client dashboard → Search & AI visibility → capture strip and throughout (/clients/[id])
whatYouSee: "Snapshot from 2026-05-12 · 20 real buyer questions · 3 of 5 AI engines measured" — a bare machine-formatted date on the client's own dashboard, with no "two months ago" and no warning that it is old. Across the report you are told we'll retry on the next snapshot, this is measured on the next snapshot, we ask every engine the same questions on every snapshot. There is no control anywhere on the page that produces a next snapshot, and no date for when one is due.
whyItsWrong: The date is emitted as a raw machine date string straight into client copy. The snapshot is only ever written by the intel pipeline, and there are exactly three entry points: client creation, the staff-only regenerate action, and the admin-only monthly schedule — which never fires for a client whose schedule was never switched on. So for any client whose admin didn't enable the schedule, the promised next snapshot never happens and the report ages silently forever, while the empty state promises a first snapshot within a day of onboarding. And while a run IS in progress, the client sees a top-of-page banner that names two staff-only controls, and the panel below keeps showing the stale snapshot with no in-place refreshing state.

src/components/seo-geo-panel.tsx:291 — rendered via buildContextLine

fix: (1) Humanize the date in src/components/seo-geo/presenter.ts:182-185 (locale month-day-year plus a relative age) and give buildContextLine a warning tone past a staleness threshold. (2) Pass `client.intelScheduleEnabled` and `client.intelScheduleNextRunAt` from src/app/(app)/clients/[id]/page.tsx:107 into SeoGeoPanel and replace the bare "next snapshot" phrases (presenter.ts:268, 365; panel 308, 375, 468) with the real date, or with an ask-us-to-schedule prompt using the existing FlagButton (src/components/seo-geo/flag-button.tsx) when the schedule is off. (3) Pass `isAiProcessingLockActive(client)` (src/lib/constants) into the panel and show an in-place "Refreshing this snapshot now" state on the capture strip at panel line 291, and drop the Regenerate / Refresh Task Map wording from the non-admin copy in src/components/ai-processing-banner.tsx:22 and 41, since a CLIENT_USER has neither control. Also mark known-bad captures: the team treats snapshots taken before the 2026-07-24 SEO/GEO redeploy as unreliable — stamp each snapshot with a pipeline version and render pre-cutoff ones with an "outdated — regenerate" banner instead of presenting them as current.

title: Urgent cards sort below important ones under a header that says the list is ordered by impact
surface: Client dashboard → Search & AI visibility → "What we're fixing" (/clients/[id])
whatYouSee: The section says it is ordered by expected impact on your scores. Then a red urgent card sits several rows below an amber important one. Scanning top-down does not give you the urgent things first.
whyItsWrong: The list is sorted by an internal impact number, but the priority chip and that number are computed on unrelated scales. Site-check rows derive both from registry weight, so the number runs 0–10 and urgent needs 7 or more. The three competitor-visibility rows set their chip independently and produce much smaller numbers: "you are never named in category answers" is flagged urgent but its number tops out at 4.5, and the citation gap tops out at 3.5. So a half-failing site check scoring 5 and tagged important outranks a genuinely urgent visibility gap. A side effect of the same threshold: any check whose registry weight is below 7 can never be urgent no matter how completely it fails.
evidence: src/components/seo-geo/presenter.ts:741-742 — `.sort((a, b) => b.scoreLift - a.scoreLift)` only
src/components/seo-geo-panel.tsx:424 — "Ordered by expected impact on your scores."

Then normalize the two lift scales in src/lib/seo-geo.ts so the visibility gaps (lines 855, 868, 881) land in the same 0–10 band as computeCheckGaps (line 804), and derive severity from the normalized lift in severityFromLift (line 744) instead of hardcoding it per gap type at lines 852, 865 and 878.

title: When the AI capture fails, the report tells the client it asked zero buyer questions
surface: Client dashboard → Search & AI visibility → capture strip, engine comparison, methodology card (/clients/[id])
whatYouSee: A degraded run renders "Snapshot from 2026-07-14 · 0 real buyer questions · 0 of 5 AI engines measured", then a card headed "You vs competitors on each AI engine" whose subtitle reads "how often each brand gets named when we ask the engines 0 real buyer questions — excluding the 0 questions that name you directly, so the comparison is like-for-like", then a collapsed row labelled "The 0 buyer questions we asked" that opens onto an empty list.
whyItsWrong: When the visibility capture rejects, the pipeline substitutes an empty probe set, empty prompt set and a one-name roster, and the panel renders the full scaffolding against those zeros. The engine-level fallback is handled — a blue banner does explain that no engine answers were captured — but the counts are interpolated into three separate sentences with no guard, and the questions disclosure invites a click that leads to an empty box. It reads like the product is broken rather than like one leg of one run degraded.

title: The report says the site was never cited and cited 11 times, on the same screen
surface: Client dashboard (/clients/[id]) — “What we're fixing” card vs the citation leaderboard
whatYouSee: A fix card reads “Site never cited as a source by Claude — What we found: Cited in 0% of category answers.” Scroll down inside the same report and the leaderboard footer reads “Your site was cited 11 times across these answers.”
whyItsWrong: Two numbers for the same measurement, both presented as fact, roughly one screen apart. One counts citations per engine across category answers; the other counts across all captured answers — but nothing on the page says so, so a client reads it as the report contradicting itself. This is the kind of thing that ends a trust conversation.
evidence: src/components/seo-geo-panel.tsx:492-496 — the leaderboard footer sentence
src/lib/seo-geo.ts — the per-engine citation gap that produces the “never cited” card
both are derived from the same run record with different denominators
fix: Pick one definition of “cited” for the client-facing report and derive both surfaces from it. If the two scopes must differ, say so in each sentence (“cited in 0 of 16 Claude category answers” vs “cited 11 times across all 60 captured answers”) so the numbers stop looking contradictory.

title: Rename the “Search engines” label — the call agreed it reads as AI search

whatYouSee: The fix list filters by All | Search engines | AI answers, and cards carry "search engines" / "search + AI" chips. On the 27 Jul review call: "What's the difference between search engine and… we should rename it, because search engines also sounds like AI."
whyItsWrong: The distinction the report hinges on — classic Google-style search versus AI assistants — is carried by a word the team itself finds ambiguous. If the people who built it pause on the label, a client will too.

title: Two of the nine signed-off v1 fixes shipped and were silently reverted by a merge the same day
surface: Client dashboard → "What we're fixing" — the whole panel
whatYouSee: On the 27 Jul review call, looking at the jargon card titles: "I thought I sent this, and it was changed." / "I don't see any change. Maybe you didn't merge it." / "No, I sent out the change." Both instincts were right: the change shipped, and a merge un-shipped it.
whyItsWrong: Commit db573d0 (22 Jul, "fix(seo-geo): QA v1 sign-off — 9 fixes + above-minimum prompt pipeline & approve flow") rendered the plain-English action plan with its working Approve button — v1 Fixes 6 and 7. Hours later, de0d414 ("fix: resolve SEO dashboard merge boundary") resolved a merge against the five-day-older SCRUM-52 redesign and kept the old panel; the fixed component became an orphan. Both files still compile, so no build, test or reviewer caught it — the plain-English copy is still generated and persisted on every run, then thrown away at render.
evidence: git db573d0 — seo-geo-panel.tsx imports and renders SeoGeoActionPlan (grep count 2), GapList 0
git de0d414 (same day) — SeoGeoActionPlan 0, GapList 2; HEAD unchanged since
src/lib/intel/seo-geo.ts:797 — recommendations still built and persisted every run
src/components/seo-geo-action-plan.tsx — complete component, zero importers
fix: Restoration is finding 1 (remount SeoGeoActionPlan — a revert-of-a-revert). Prevention is the real fix: a CI check that fails when an exported component has zero importers (or a panel smoke test asserting recommendations render), and a rule that any merge touching seo-geo-panel.tsx re-runs the v1 sign-off checklist. Without it, the next merge can un-ship the fix again.
